subject: AnchorBridge private-connectivity — intermittent path failures and SG/NAT interplay
messages:
From: Adam Shore <adam.shore@anchorbridge.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: ops@anchorbridge.com
Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Intermittent TCP failures into our private gateway (GRE)

Hi Karthik —

We started seeing intermittent failures this morning for traffic from our on-prem app cluster into the Redwood Private VPC. Symptoms: long-lived TCP sessions (DB replication and file syncs) get stalled after ~30–90s. When it happens we see retransmits and then a bunch of blackholed packets.

What we've captured so far:
- Attached a short pcap from the AnchorBridge edge (anchorbridge-trace-20261207.pcap).
- Traceroute from our host to a Private VPC ip: shows an MTU-advice ICMP at one hop but no subsequent path MTU reduction.
- We see the sessions come up, then packets stop flowing back from the Private side.

We suspect one of: MTU/fragmentation being silently dropped, asymmetric return path (on-prem firewall returning via different hop and hitting SNAT/SG mismatch), or a conntrack/NAT table overflow causing state loss.

Can you loop in network infra? We're starting to see customer impact. Happy to hop on a call and hand off the pcap.

Attachments: anchorbridge-trace-20261207.pcap

—Adam Shore
NetOps, AnchorBridge
adam.shore@anchorbridge.com
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Intermittent TCP failures into our private gateway (GRE)

Thanks Adam — I've got the pcap and started an initial review. Looping Vanessa and Marissa from Private Connectivity and Edge infra.

First-pass notes:
- I can see lots of ICMP "frag needed" messages in the pcap that don't appear to be acted on (no subsequent smaller-fragment packets). That suggests an intermediate drop of ICMP or MTU/PMTU policy not applied.
- I also see repeated SYN/ACK retransmits from the Private side followed by what looks like SNAT retry behavior. Could be asymmetric return path.

Next steps I propose:
1) Vanessa — can you confirm current SG/ACLs on the Private border for AnchorBridge routes and whether ICMP (type 3/code 4) is allowed?
2) Marissa — can you capture conntrack/NAT table snapshot on the Private egress node for the timeframe (if possible) and attach?
3) Adam — can you run a traceroute -M/pmtu from your host to our endpoint and paste results?

If we see blocked ICMP, we'll need to allow fragmentation-needed or implement MSS clamp on the Firewall as a short-term workaround. If asymmetric routing is present we should pin a return route or add a static SNAT rule for the affected prefix.

I'll stand up a call if we need a fast remediation window.

-karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Network Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: ops@anchorbridge.com
Date: Wed, 08 Dec 2026 08:34:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent TCP failures into our private gateway (GRE)

Karthik/Vanessa — I pulled the NAT/conntrack snapshot for the egress node that handles AnchorBridge (attached: nat-table-snapshot-20261208.txt). High-level findings:
- NAT table shows a handful of short-lived entries in rapid churn for the AnchorBridge prefix; many of the session tuples are being rewritten by a secondary route table when return traffic takes the non-primary path.
- Conntrack timeouts are default values; a few large bulk transfers caused ephemeral port reuse that exposed the missing sticky NAT binding when the return path changed.

Immediate mitigation suggestions:
- Add a temporary static SNAT mapping for the AnchorBridge prefix to force return flows through the same egress node.
- Alternatively, if we can ensure ICMP frag-needed passes end-to-end, add MSS clamp on the on-prem-facing firewall to avoid fragmentation.

I've included the NAT snapshot as requested. We should coordinate a 30-min maintenance window to apply the SNAT stickiness and monitor. If Adam can confirm traceroute/ICMP blocking, we'll pick the option with least customer impact.

Attachment: nat-table-snapshot-20261208.txt

—Marissa Cole
Connectivity Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Adam Shore <adam.shore@anchorbridge.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Thanks Marissa. Traceroute and MTU results below (from our app host to 10.120.45.7):

1  10.0.0.1  1.1 ms  1.0 ms  0.9 ms
2  172.16.4.1  2.4 ms  2.2 ms  2.1 ms
3  100.64.12.5  5.7 ms  5.6 ms  5.6 ms  (ICMP frag-needed seen here; MTU suggested 1388)
4  10.120.45.7  8.2 ms  8.0 ms  8.1 ms

We do see the frag-needed on hop 3, but our packets are not being retransmitted at a smaller size. We also verified our edge firewall blocks inbound ICMP type 3 code 4 by default (policy from older security posture). I've uploaded the SG audit for your reference.

Attachment: sg-audit-20261208.txt

If you enable ICMP frag-needed through your path, we should see correct PMTU behaviour. If you prefer not to adjust SGs quickly, we can apply MSS clamp on our firewall as a workaround (we can schedule a small config change on our side if Redwood confirms the clamp value).

We can take the maintenance window as early as Thu 2026-12-09 02:00 UTC.

—Adam
From: priyom_das@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Adam Shore <adam.shore@anchorbridge.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Remediation play: SG allow + MSS clamp + SNAT sticky mapping

Proposed remedial steps (we should pick one path and rollback plan):

Option A (preferred fast path) — enable ICMP frag-needed and monitor
- Add explicit SG rule allowing ICMP type 3 code 4 between AnchorBridge prefix and Private VPC ingress.
- Remove after 24h if no regressions.
- Rollback: remove the SG rule.

Option B (if SG change requires policy approval) — MSS clamp + SNAT stickiness
- On AnchorBridge firewall: set MSS clamp to 1360 for sessions to Private VPC prefixes (prevents fragmentation). We coordinate the exact iptables/ASA command with AnchorBridge.
- On Redwood egress node: add a static SNAT entry mapping AnchorBridge prefix -> ephemeral SNAT range on primary egress to preserve return path.
- Validation: verify replication sessions remain stable for 15 continuous minutes; watch conntrack churn.
- Rollback: remove static SNAT and revert MSS clamp.

Command snippets (example):
- iptables --table mangle --append FORWARD --src <anchorbridge-prefix> --dst <private-prefix> -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --set-mss 1360
- redwood-netctl nat add static-snat --src-prefix <anchorbridge-prefix> --snat-ip 10.7.255.42 --node primary-egress-2

I'll be available during the Thu maintenance window. If Adam can confirm MSS clamp on their side is possible, we can do the full fix together.

—Priyom Das
Edge Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
